title: Session 2 — Participant 16 User + Claude Behavior Graphs
goal: Improve the results chapter as per the roadmap provided by Claude in Session 1.
context:
The goal of session 2 of this project is to further improve, the already written results chapter as per the roadmap provided by Claude in session 1. Claude will be used as an AI agent to quantify fluorescence images. Claude will also be used to design graphs and create a scientific illustration (graphical abstract) for the manuscript and finally proofread the manuscript. I will use my academic knowledge to analyse, validate, and approve Claude’s suggestions and integrate them into the results chapter. This will make this paper easy to understand for non-scientific readers and will make it ready for publication.
This session is different from Session 1 as it will use an AI-generated (Claude-generated) prompt to create a Graphical abstract using another AI (BioRender AI); a recently added feature in BioRender. The task can be challenging as well as interesting at the same time.
Although the goal of Session 2 was the natural flow in my mind, some of the tasks were influenced by the use of AI agent (roadmap) provided in Session 1.
occupation: Teaching and Research Professor and Chairperson of the Department of Biotechnology.

session_goal_achievement.Why or why not: The interaction was over one and a half hours. All of the 5 tasks proposed in today’s session are achieved. A fluorescent image of the cells is quantified and represented in terms of a graph, a summary of the result is now added at the end of the chapter, and a graphical abstract is now created and will be used at the time of submission. The over all cnsitancy of the chapter is double-checked, and the suggestions will be incorporated into the paper.

Step 1.step_action: The required picture upload (Figure 5), along with its caption. Prompt Claude to analyse and quantify the picture based on the information in the caption. Convert the data into a table (Excel format).

nodes.label: Frame the apoptosis-quantification task for Claude
nodes.detail: Explains today's goal of converting a fluorescence-microscopy figure into a scored-percentage table, then uploads Figure 5 and its caption, asking Claude to build a 4-row table (viable/early apoptotic/late apoptotic/necrotic) across the four treatment panels for use in GraphPad Prism.

nodes.label: Refuse to generate percentages by visual estimation
nodes.detail: Explains it should not fabricate per-cell counts or percentages by eye from a fluorescence image, since that would present invented numbers as real measurements. Proposes the scientifically defensible alternative: opening the image in ImageJ/Fiji and using the Cell Counter plugin.

nodes.label: Review Claude's response about Refuse to generate percentages by visual estimation
Prefer visual quantification over ImageJ, request illustrative table from image
Offer faster manual-counting alternatives without lowering rigor
nodes.detail: Suggests lighter-weight ways to get real counts without a full ImageJ Cell Counter session -- a quick manual tally on paper (5-15 minutes), or counting a representative sub-region when cell density is high -- while maintaining that the numbers must come from an actual count.

nodes.label: Review Claude's response about Offer faster manual-counting alternatives without lowering rigor
Argue for expert visual classification and propose labeling values as illustrative
nodes.detail: Pushes back that an experienced scientist visually classifying and counting cells under the microscope is a legitimate method, and that the resulting values could be labeled as illustrative rather than measured. Offers a compromise to mark the visually-estimated percentages in the manuscript as illustrative and not representing actual measured values.

nodes.label: Decline the disclaimer workaround and offer legitimate alternatives
nodes.detail: Explains that an 'illustrative, not real' disclaimer does not make fabricated numbers acceptable in a Results section, since journals treat any invented quantitative result as fabrication regardless of caveats. Offers two real alternatives instead: a qualitative prose comparison across panels, or staying on the call while the user performs a genuine live tally that Claude organizes into a table in real time.

nodes.label: Review Claude's response about Decline the disclaimer workaround and offer legitimate alternatives
Defend visual counting as legitimate, invite Claude to try
Push back: Claude's image-derived percentages are estimates, not legitimate visual counts
Review Claude's response about Push back: Claude's image-derived percentages are estimates, not legitimate visual counts
Decide to count manually and submit extracted percentage data
nodes.detail: Decides to do the manual cell counting independently rather than on the call, noting that ImageJ can be tried later if there is time, then sends Claude the percentage values he extracted for the four treatment panels.

nodes.label: Question whether the data reflects a genuine manual tally
nodes.detail: Asks whether these specific numbers came from an actual manual count or from another AI's visual estimate of the image, explaining that routing the same visual-estimation problem through a different AI would not make it legitimate. Requests the raw per-panel cell counts rather than pre-converted percentages.

nodes.label: Review Claude's response about Question whether the data reflects a genuine manual tally
Explain the real counting methodology and finalize the table
nodes.detail: Clarifies that the counts came from a genuine manual tally of roughly 100 cells scored by area per representative image, which Claude accepts as legitimate quantification (n≈100 conveniently maps closely to percentage points). The percentage table is finalized on this basis rather than through ImageJ.

Step 2.step_name: Conversion of tabulated data into a publication-quality graph with a scientifically accurate caption.
Step 2.step_action: Prompt Claude to suggest the best graph design. Upload data to GraphPad Prism. Graph design selection. Graph creation and Claude approval.

nodes.label: Ask Claude to recommend a graph design for the percentage table
nodes.detail: Asks whether a stacked-column or an individual-value graph would best visualize the new viable/apoptotic/necrotic percentage table.

nodes.label: Recommend a 100% stacked column graph
nodes.detail: Recommends a 100% stacked column graph (composition per treatment) over individual columns, since the latter would make the chart too congested with four categories across four treatments.

nodes.label: Review Claude's response about Recommend a 100% stacked column graph
Build and export the stacked-bar graph in GraphPad Prism
nodes.detail: Creates a new grouped data table in Prism, enters the percentage data with the 'enter and plot error values already calculated' option, selects the stacked-bars summary format, adjusts the y-axis to a proper 0-100% scale and tweaks bar colors for visual distinction, then exports the finished chart as an image file.

nodes.label: Add export graph in Results Chapter_modified
Upload the finished graph and request a caption
nodes.detail: Uploads the exported graph image (Data 2.tif) back into the Claude chat and asks for a ready-to-use figure caption.

nodes.label: Draft a scientifically grounded figure caption
nodes.detail: Drafts a caption stating the classification is based on a minimum of ~100 cells scored per treatment from representative fields, then flags its own assumptions for the user to confirm: the figure number, and the deliberate omission of mean±SD since this is a single representative field rather than triplicate fields.

nodes.label: Review Claude's response about Draft a scientifically grounded figure caption
Check Results Chapter_modified
Clarify counting method: ~100 cells per field counted under microscope, use 100 as base
Validate microscope count as legitimate, suggest methods wording, and provide figure caption
Confirm the caption and figure placement
nodes.detail: Reviews Claude's notes on figure numbering and the single-field assumption, and confirms/adjusts the details before accepting the caption as ready to place into the chapter as Figure 5B.

nodes.label: Add caption in Results Chapter_modified and change the font

Step 3.step_name: Write a short closing summary paragraph for the whole Results chapter and find highly active compounds.
Step 3.step_action: Ask Claude to review all the edits and write a short paragraph of the results chapter highlighting the major findings.

nodes.label: Request the closing summary paragraph suggested in Session 1
nodes.detail: Reminds Claude that it had previously suggested adding a short closing summary paragraph to the Results chapter, and asks it to generate one now.

nodes.label: Request the real chapter file and propose a paragraph structure
nodes.detail: Explains it would rather work from the actual updated chapter file than reconstruct numeric details (IC50, DNA-fragmentation, hemolysis) from memory of the conversation, to avoid numeric errors. Lays out a 5-part structure (opening scope, potency summary, selectivity summary, mechanistic thread, closing framing sentence) so the user knows what to expect.

nodes.label: Review Claude's response about Request the real chapter file and propose a paragraph structure
Report progress and upload the current chapter
nodes.detail: Reports the changes made so far (corrected nomenclature, added graphs and quantitative analysis), notes that DNA-fragmentation analysis is not yet done, and saves and uploads the current version of the results chapter for Claude to work from.

nodes.label: Identify the best-performing compounds and draft the summary
nodes.detail: Without being told which compound to favor, reads the uploaded chapter and drafts a closing paragraph identifying MS26Vin2 and MS26Me3 as the two most potent, non-hemolytic lead compounds among the twelve screened.

nodes.label: Review Claude's response about Identify the best-performing compounds and draft the summary
Request more emphasis on the two lead compounds
nodes.detail: Asks for a revision that keeps the same overall length but gives more emphasis to the two lead compounds identified.

nodes.label: Produce the tightened, lead-compound-focused paragraph
nodes.detail: Rewrites the paragraph to foreground MS26Vin2 and MS26Me3 as the standout compounds, tying together their potency, selectivity, and morphological/apoptotic findings.

nodes.label: Check and approve the paragraph and paste it into the chapter
nodes.detail: Accepts the revised paragraph and pastes it into the Results Chapter Word document, saving it for later light copyediting.

Step 4.step_action: Upload the result summary; prompt Claude to create a simple illustration (graphical abstract) that can be drawn in BioRender.

nodes.label: Request a graphical abstract concept and a BioRender-ready prompt
nodes.detail: Asks Claude to keep it as simple as possible: generate a graphical abstract that could be drawn in BioRender, and separately provide a caption/prompt that could be fed to BioRender AI to generate the figure automatically and save time.

nodes.label: Draft an initial schematic diagram and a descriptive prompt
nodes.detail: Produces its own simple schematic (untreated -> drug treatment -> rounded/apoptotic -> apoptotic bodies -> DNA fragmentation, non-hemolytic to host RBCs) plus a descriptive caption/prompt intended for use with BioRender AI.

nodes.label: Review Claude's response about Draft an initial schematic diagram and a descriptive prompt
Accept Claude to generate a rough visual mockup
Generate a rough visual mockup
Explore BioRender's AI illustration tools
nodes.detail: Opens BioRender and browses its built-in AI icon/illustration tools (Apply BioRender Style, Restyle Icon, Remove Background, Custom Edit) while reviewing what Claude has produced so far.

nodes.label: Reject Claude's schematic, request full illustration from screening to mechanism
nodes.detail: Rejects Claude's plain schematic as not a real illustration, asking instead for a complete image covering screening of compounds through to mechanism of killing and results.

nodes.label: Generate image rather than schematic representation
Review Claude's response about Generate image rather than schematic representation
Request full graphical abstract from screening to mechanism, to be uploaded into BioRender AI
Generate full graphical abstract
Pass Claude's caption prompt into BioRender AI to generate figure
nodes.detail: Pastes Claude's descriptive caption directly into BioRender AI's 'Generate Editable Figure' tool.

nodes.label: Generate BioRender-style illustration previews
nodes.detail: Generates three preview illustrations from the pasted prompt, depicting Leishmania tropica promastigote -> organotin(IV) treatment -> morphological change (shrinkage/rounding/loss of flagellum) -> apoptosis-like death (AO/EB staining shift, DNA fragmentation) -> parasite death, with a non-hemolytic-to-human-RBCs callout.

nodes.label: Select and convert the best preview into an editable figure
nodes.detail: Chooses the strongest of the three generated previews, converts it to an editable BioRender figure, and rates how close it is to a final, usable figure.

nodes.label: Manually refine and export the illustration
nodes.detail: Refines the editable figure directly on the BioRender canvas -- regrouping elements and repositioning the AO/EB-staining and DNA-fragmentation panels -- and exports a PNG version, checking the saved file in the local downloads folder.

nodes.label: Review Claude's response about Generate full graphical abstract and decide to go with the BioRender
Add the export illustration to Results Chapter_modified
Ask Claude whether it likes the export GA
Flag a disconnected outcome and propose a single connecting arrow
nodes.detail: Reviews the re-uploaded illustration and flags that fixing the earlier ambiguous forked arrow left 'Parasite death' visually disconnected from the rest of the sequence, recommending a single arrow linking the AO/EB panel down to Parasite death so it reads as the final step in one continuous chain.

nodes.label: Review Claude's response about Flag a disconnected outcome and propose a single connecting arrow
Apply another fix and re-upload
Give another arrow suggestion
Review Claude's response about Give another arrow suggestion and refuse the suggestion from Claude
Edit the figure and download it
Ask Claude whether it likes the update GA
Approve the corrected sequential flow
nodes.detail: Confirms the fix works: the sequence now reads correctly as morphology change -> DNA fragmentation -> parasite death, with the AO/EB staining shift as confirmatory evidence beneath it.

nodes.label: Review Claude's response about Approve the corrected sequential flow and GA
Ask Claude to visually point out a flagged detail
nodes.detail: Asks Claude to circle/highlight a specific fix in the image as a visual annotation rather than describing it in text.

nodes.label: Attempt to pinpoint the flagged element, then self-correct
nodes.detail: Crops and inspects the region around the flagged label to locate and circle the element, but on closer inspection cannot actually find the artifact it had described, and corrects itself and apologizes for the mis-description.

nodes.label: Change the picture in Results Chapter_modified
Finalize the graphical abstract and reflect on the workflow
nodes.detail: Confirms the graphical abstract is finished and approved, noting a task that normally takes about two hours was completed in roughly fifteen minutes with this AI-assisted workflow, and reiterates it will be used only as a submission-portal abstract image, not part of the chapter itself.

Step 5.step_action: Ask Claude to review all the edits, check for consistency, compare results, check the quality of figures, analyze images, captions, units, numbering and unsupported statements.

nodes.label: Request a full consistency and cross-validation review
nodes.detail: Declares this the session's final task, uploads the complete updated results chapter, and asks Claude to review all edits for consistency, figure/caption quality, units, numbering, and unsupported statements -- clarifying that the graphical abstract sits at the end only as a future submission-abstract image, not part of the chapter proper.

nodes.label: Process and scrutinize the uploaded chapter
nodes.detail: Converts and reads through the newly uploaded chapter in full, scrutinizing table values, unit formatting, and the hemolysis section for inconsistencies.

nodes.label: Free up system resources while Claude works
nodes.detail: Signs out of BioRender while waiting for Claude's review to complete.

nodes.label: Stop Claude and fix the prompt since haven't uploaded the chapter
Deliver the consistency report
nodes.detail: Returns a consistency report confirming most of the session's edits are correct, while flagging a few remaining issues: some unit-symbol formatting, a missing table cross-reference/citation, and a minor grammar issue.

nodes.label: Review the report and close the session
nodes.detail: Reviews the flagged issues, accepts that most edits are correct, decides to fix the remaining items after the recorded session rather than now, and closes the session.
